title: Embedding fairness: weighted scheduling, soft-throttles, and capacity-aware admission
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem summary: embedding endpoints see large tenant variance in burstiness and request size (short vectors vs n-shot batches). Current single FIFO queue + binary rate-limiter causes noisy neighbor effects: high-volume tenants monopolize warm pools, causing p95/p99 latency spikes for other customers and reactive autoscaler churn. This ticket defines a multi-pronged runtime change: (1) introduce tenant-weighted priority queues with fairness windows, (2) implement soft-throttle (decay token bucket) per-tenant group to smooth bursts without hard drops, and (3) make admission and autoscaling SLO-aware by combining observed queue_time percentiles with capacity headroom signals for scale decisions and capacity planning forecasts.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes weighted-queue config per routing key with at least 3 QoS classes (low/standard/high) and tenant-weight override.
Soft-throttle implemented as a decay-token bucket that reduces instantaneous admitted concurrency rather than rejecting requests; default smoothing window configurable.
Autoscaler uses queue_time_p95 and p99 plus node-utilization to decide scale-up/scale-down; scale-down conservative hysteresis added to avoid oscillation.
E2E benchmarks showing p99 latency improvement of >=25% for median tenants during synthetic burst tests while tail for high-volume tenants remains within SLA.
Load tests and canary deployment runbook documented with rollback criteria and monitoring dashboards linked.
Dashboard shows per-tenant "fairness_score", queue_time percentiles, admitted_rate, and throttle_events over time.
Runbook created for production incidents: steps to adjust tenant weights, temporarily increase headroom, and emergency hard-drop thresholds.
tasks: Design: define tenant-weight formula (combination of committed QPS, historical 95th token/sec, and business priority).
Engineering: implement multi-queue scheduler in embedding front-tier (non-blocking, lock-free where possible).
Engineering: build decay-token-bucket soft-throttle library with tunable half-life and emergency clamp.
Autoscaler: add queue-time p95/p99 signals and capacity headroom heuristic; integrate with current provisioner.
Testing: create synthetic arrival generator for mixed tenant profiles (spiky, steady, large-batch).
Benchmarking: run cluster-level experiments against baseline to measure latency, throughput, and cost delta.
Observability: update console dashboard and tracing hooks; instrument fairness_score and throttle_events.
Docs & Runbook: publish architecture proposal, rollout plan, and incident playbook to Confluence.

notes: Design trade-offs discussed: strict WFQ (weighted fair queuing) provides theoretical fairness but is expensive on lock contention; chosen approach uses per-thread queues with periodic redistribution to approximate WFQ to reduce latency overhead.
Cost considerations: smoothing reduces peak GPU utilization but may increase tail-cost due to longer overall processing time; include cost monitoring in benchmarks to track cost per 1k embeddings.
Operational knobs exposed: tenant_weight, qos_class, throttle_half_life_sec, emergency_drop_threshold, autoscaler_queue_p99_threshold.
